cognate: Av. āp- 'water' ~ Latv. upe 'river' (Lith. upė, OPr. ape) < *h₂ep-; Av. tak- (tacaiti, ptc. tacint-) ~ Latv. tecēt/tek (Lith. tekėti, Slav. teči) < *tekʷ- 'run'. Both members cognate. (The āp-/upe and tak-/tecēt etymologies are standard dictionary etymology. The collocation itself comes from the passages, not from the literature.)
drift_or_renewal: Noun: 'water' (Iranian) vs 'river' (Baltic), a small specialisation of *h₂ep-. Verb: in both, *tekʷ- 'run' is used of water. That shift is near-universal (cf. Lat. currere, Gmc. rinnan of rivers), so it is not diagnostic by itself. What matters is the pairing of two cognates plus the grain context below. Vedic has no ap- + tak- collocation (checked RV), and Slavic keeps teči of rivers (Slovo: Двина ... течетъ, orv:spi 143 in B-399b8) but has renewed *h₂ep- as reka.
shared_syntax: *h₂ep- is the subject (Latv. upe tek, Av. āpō taciṇti) or carries the participle as an attribute (Av. āpəm taciṇtąm, tacat̰ āpa): the water/river is what 'runs'.
context: The Avestan anchor pairs the flowing water with grain: VS19.26c āpəm taciṇtąm yauuanąm uruϑmąm, 'the flowing water, the growth of grains'. The slab maps yauuanąm to 'young', but it is from yauua- 'grain' = Skt. yáva-. The Yasna litany has the same pairing with plants: Y16.8 tacat̰ āpa uxšiiat̰ uruuara, 'flowing water, growing plants'. The Latvian anchors pair the running river with grain in the same breath: lv:p0518 Tek upe caur namu ... tā tek mieži, rudzi ('the river runs through the house; so run barley and rye'); lv:BV 28155 Tīru rudzu upe tek ('a river of pure rye runs'). The river as an image of agrarian abundance (also lv:BV 30972: vīna upe tek, a river of wine, a river of silver). So both traditions use cognate *h₂ep- + *tekʷ- in traditional diction about fertility, coupled with grain or plants. A generic 'river flows' would not explain that. Still low: both words are the everyday terms in each language, and the Latvian corpus could not be searched beyond the slab.

note: Slab is mostly Old Russian chronicle prose paired by automatic root matches (posla/muži ~ OE sealdon/monna, molitisę bogu ~ RV bhágaḥ...mr̥dhyāḥ, gorodъ ~ AV gṛhā). These are recurring false positives with no shared wording. One low-confidence claim: Avestan āp- + tak- ~ Latvian upe tek. I considered and rejected: ORV idete domovi ~ Lat. i domum (bare goal case with *h₁ei-, generic syntax); ORV zvězdy i nebo ~ Latv. zvaigzne debesīs (biblical and generic); OE on geweald gesellan ~ ORV dati vlastь (translationese); Slovo 'grey wolves seeking honour and glory', which has no partner wording. Latvian dainas could not be searched beyond the slab because their source is under raw/books (off limits).
